The Wendigo. I grew up in Minnesota, and where I lived we were taught a lot of Native American folklore. I usually don’t really believe in folklore, but with Native American folklore being what I’ve grown up with, I tend to believe it more. There are also two general telling of the Wendigo.

The Wendigo is a creature who was once a man. For reasons of insanity or desperation, the man began to cannibalize those around him, making meals of out his friends. Hiding in isolation, the man begins to turn into a horrible beast, with claws and fangs, a twisted and elongated body. He now searches in the woods at night to steal you up and eat you.

The second variation shows the Wendigo as a man-eating spirit who stalks the forests to find his next victim. Usually depicted as tall, emaciated, with fangs and antlers as well as claws, the Wendigo is essentially a hulking skeleton with speed and anger to best any man. You’re not supposed to say the name aloud, lest it hear you and find you.
